Meta's trailing-twelve-month capital expenditure on data centers reached roughly $19 billion as of March 2026, up from $6.4 billion two years earlier, a near-tripling that places physical infrastructure at the center of its competitive position.

The year-on-year pattern is unambiguous. Spend held roughly flat between the periods ending March 2023 and March 2024, then jumped to $12.9 billion by March 2025 and $19.0 billion by March 2026. That acceleration maps directly onto the demand for compute: more GPUs require more buildings, more cooling, and more grid capacity to house and power them. The data does not say how that spending breaks down across land, construction, and electrical infrastructure, but the scale of the increase implies commitments well beyond equipment procurement alone.

Within this peer group, Meta sits fourth. Amazon leads at $54.2 billion, followed by Alphabet at $35.7 billion and Microsoft at $30.9 billion. CoreWeave, a pure-play GPU cloud, is already at $7.7 billion despite being a fraction of Meta's age and revenue base. Equinix and Digital Realty, the colocation specialists, trail the hyperscalers by a wide margin, which reflects the difference between owning compute capacity and providing the buildings that house it. The data covers only the most recent trailing-twelve-month figure for peers, so trajectory comparisons across the group are not possible here.
